speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please describe the painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg in detail, including when it started and how it appeared.

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your history of Crohn's disease, diabetes, and the recall of an insect bite, I need to clarify the lesion's current characteristics: Is the wound edge raised and rolled, and is there any discharge or surrounding redness? Also, have you noticed any fever or chills recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum secondary to Crohn's disease.

The central necrotic base with purplish irregular borders, history of Crohn's, and the "pathergy" phenomenon (lesion appearing/progressing after an ant bite) are classic features. The pitting edema and dilated veins suggest concurrent venous insufficiency, but the ulcer morphology points to an underlying neutrophilic dermatosis. I am not requesting further tests as the clinical picture is sufficient for this diagnosis.
